problem: SSRF: the diff removes the ALLOWED_HOSTS check and the fixed https://api.internal.example/ base. The caller's string is now passed straight to requests.get(user_url), so any URL gets fetched and its body is returned.
failure: fetch_report('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/') returns the cloud metadata credentials. 'http://localhost:6379/' or 'http://10.0.0.5/admin' return internal service responses instead of raising ValueError('host not allowed').
fix: Bring back the fixed https base with path-only input and the hostname allowlist check. If full URLs are truly needed, check the scheme, the host against the allowlist, and the resolved IP (reject private, loopback and link-local), and set allow_redirects=False or re-check every redirect hop.

problem: No scheme check. The old code always built an https:// URL, but the new code accepts http:// and any other scheme that requests can handle, so report fetches can go out in plaintext.
failure: fetch_report('http://api.internal.example/report') sends the request unencrypted, where it can be read or changed in transit. The old code always used https.
fix: Require urlparse(url).scheme == 'https', or go back to building the URL from the fixed https base.

problem: Breaking contract: the parameter changed from a relative `path`, resolved against api.internal.example, to a full `user_url`. The function name and return type stayed the same, so existing callers break silently.
failure: A caller that still runs fetch_report('reports/2026/q3.pdf') now gets requests.exceptions.MissingSchema instead of the report bytes.
fix: Keep the `path: str` signature and its behavior, or rename the function and update every caller.

problem: resp.content reads the whole body into memory with no size limit. Before this change the target was a fixed trusted host; now the attacker picks it.
failure: If user_url points to a multi-GB file or an endless streaming endpoint, resp.content buffers all of it. The 10s timeout only limits the gap between reads, so the worker can run out of memory.
fix: Restore the trusted fixed host. Otherwise use stream=True and stop reading once the body passes a maximum byte count.
